minutes.headline: Select Board authorized final payment to the school project contractor while pursuing the HVAC and roof design engineers.
minutes.summary: The board heard State Rep. Benson on local aid, circuit breaker, the housing bill and Unitil bills, then took up school project closeout, where members disputed heating and roof problems. They ratified a police officer appointment, reviewed draft annual Town Meeting articles, adopted a pregnant workers policy, and debated economic development next steps before going into executive session on a DPW union matter.

Enter executive session under section 21 reason 3 on collective bargaining regarding the DPW union, not to return to public session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to authorize final payment to the school project's general contractor and to pursue the design engineers for the heating system and the roof.
The board learned that town counsel advised withholding the contractor's final payment was not possible; members disputed the heating and roof problems.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a full-time police officer, effective March 30, 2018.
The board reviewed draft Annual Town Meeting articles, including a snow and ice deficit amendment, the FY19 capital plan, and sewer, solid waste, water and cable budgets.
On economic development, the board leaned toward meeting the Agricultural Commission next and reached no resolution; the vote on the pregnant workers policy was not audible.

why_it_matters: The final payment closes out the middle/high school project, and pursuing the design engineers is the route by which the town may seek to recover the cost of heating and roof problems, which would otherwise fall on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The draft Town Meeting articles are the budget items residents will be asked to vote on, including the capital plan and the sewer, water and solid waste budgets.
watch_next: Town counsel's answer on conflict of interest and rule of necessity for the Hickory Hills article, before Town Meeting.
Scheduling of the Agricultural Commission meeting on economic development and of the parks, agriculture and conservation workshops.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the Lachance appointment, the state aid percentages, the final payment and the main scheduling decisions. They differ on the outcome of the final-payment and pregnant workers votes, which our minutes record as passed and not audible while the official minutes record them as not stated and passed.
